answer: River dye pulse: one $24 bottle of rhodamine tracer per identity, poured at a named willow on the bank of a single river reach. The USGS gauging station downstream logs the pigment pulse on its fluorometer, and the pulse must arrive when the river's flow says it should — a paper release shows nothing, and a single pulse claimed by two names fails them both. A flood can wash a reach out, so the station re-tests after high water.
